report-a-bug.title: Your user reports a bug
report-a-bug.summary: What the person using your app sees: one button, one sentence, and the screen goes with it.

chapters.title: Your user taps + in the cart
chapters.detail: The total turns into $NaN. Most people would close the tab and never tell you.

chapters.title: They tap the bug button in the corner
chapters.detail: That is the Mushi Mushi widget: one script tag or one npm package in your app.

chapters.title: They say what went wrong, in their own words
chapters.detail: Pick a kind and type one sentence. No account, no form to learn.

chapters.title: They tap Screenshot to attach the screen
chapters.detail: The page and what they tapped go with every report. Only you, the developer, see them.

chapters.title: They press Send. That is the whole job for them
chapters.detail: The report lands in your Mushi Mushi console, where it is explained in plain English.

bug-to-fix.title: From a bug report to a merged fix
bug-to-fix.summary: A real bug from Mushi Mushi’s own console: the plain-English diagnosis, the fix prompt for your editor, and the pull request that fixed it.

chapters.title: Every bug lands in one list
chapters.detail: Reports from your users, Sentry errors and Mushi Mushi’s own checks, ranked by how bad they are.

chapters.title: Search for a bug and open it
chapters.detail: Or start from the top of “Fix first”.

chapters.title: Read the bug in plain English
chapters.detail: Mushi Mushi rewrites the report so anyone can tell what is wrong, and rates how bad it is.

chapters.title: See why it broke and how to fix it
chapters.detail: The diagnosis names the cause, the fix and the steps to see it happen. It read 5 files of the repo to get there.

chapters.title: Hand the fix to your AI editor
chapters.detail: Copy one prompt into Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf or Lovable, or let your editor fetch it over MCP.

chapters.title: Or let an agent open the pull request
chapters.detail: A fix agent writes the change, CI runs, and a second AI reviews it against the report before it merges.

chapters.title: Check how it reached the diagnosis
chapters.detail: Every step from the report to the merged fix, with how sure Mushi Mushi was at each one.

connect-editor.title: Connect your AI editor
connect-editor.summary: Pick your editor, add Mushi Mushi in one click or one command, then ask it to fix the latest bug.

chapters.title: Pick the editor you use
chapters.detail: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Zed, or any MCP client.

chapters.title: Add Mushi Mushi in one step
chapters.detail: Claude Code gets one command to paste. Cursor and VS Code get a button that opens the install dialog.

chapters.title: Then ask your editor for the fix
chapters.detail: “Get the latest Mushi Mushi bug and fix it.” Your editor reads the diagnosis and the fix prompt for you.

chapters.title: Prefer the terminal? Use the CLI
chapters.detail: mushi reports, mushi fix, and the same data as the console.

ship-fixes.title: Watch every fix ship
ship-fixes.summary: The Pipeline page follows every bug from the report to the deploy, and shows the ones that need you.

chapters.title: Follow each bug through eight stages
chapters.detail: Reported, triaged, fix PR, reviewed, CI, release train, merged, deployed.

chapters.title: Approved fixes ship together in a release train
chapters.detail: One branch, one CI run, one merge and one deploy, instead of one per fix.

chapters.title: Anything stuck says why, with the button to move it
chapters.detail: Close it, send it back to an agent, or re-run CI, right from the list.

home-today.title: Your app on one page
home-today.summary: Home shows what needs you, what is shipping, which pages have bugs and who can reach the app.

chapters.title: Needs you lists what is waiting on you
chapters.detail: Each line says how many and why, and its button opens that list.

chapters.title: Release shows what is shipping
chapters.detail: Fix ready, CI, the release train, merged and deployed, and the last train that went out.

chapters.title: Pages shows where the bugs are
chapters.detail: Each page of your app with its visits and bug reports, so the busiest broken page comes first.

chapters.title: Check who and what can reach the app
chapters.detail: The repo, the people on the app, the SDK version, and every key with when it was last used.

chapters.title: Compare this week with last week
chapters.detail: Bug reports, critical bugs, fixes merged and visits, side by side.

fixes-queue.title: Every fix, from the first try to the merge
fixes-queue.summary: The Fixes page shows what is ready to merge, why fixes stopped, and what waits in the merge queue.

chapters.title: The top line says where things stand
chapters.detail: Ready to merge, stopped, and fixed in the last 30 days. Each number opens its list.

chapters.title: See why fixes stopped
chapters.detail: Stopped reports are grouped by reason. Retry the ones a retry can fix; the others say why not.

chapters.title: Approved fixes wait in the merge queue
chapters.detail: A second AI reviews every pull request. Approved ones ride the next release train; held ones say what they need.

chapters.title: Filter the list and open any fix
chapters.detail: Each row has the pull request, its CI and what the AI review said.

connect-tools.title: Connect the tools you already use
connect-tools.summary: GitHub for fix pull requests, Slack or Discord for alerts, Sentry for errors: one Integrations page.

chapters.title: See every connection at a glance
chapters.detail: Green is working, orange needs you, grey is not set up yet.

chapters.title: GitHub is the one Mushi Mushi needs
chapters.detail: Fixes arrive as draft pull requests on the repository you pick.

chapters.title: Get bug alerts in Slack
chapters.detail: Add Mushi Mushi to Slack, then pick which events post: new bugs, fixes opened, fixes merged.

chapters.title: Bring Sentry errors into the same list
chapters.detail: New Sentry issues are imported on their own, and closed in Sentry when the fix ships.

settings-limits.title: Set it up once in Settings
settings-limits.summary: Where bug alerts go, how bugs are sorted, and how much Mushi Mushi may spend.

chapters.title: Send a test bug any time
chapters.detail: It checks the whole path, from the widget to the diagnosis.

chapters.title: Choose where bug alerts go
chapters.detail: A Slack channel with Triage and Fix buttons, or a simple webhook.

chapters.title: Tune how bugs are sorted
chapters.detail: Which AI models run, and how alike two reports must be to become one row.

chapters.title: Cap what Mushi Mushi can spend
chapters.detail: A monthly AI budget, an auto-fix limit, fixes per day, and a price above which it asks you first.

todo-list.title: Start your day in To-do
todo-list.summary: Everything in Mushi Mushi that needs a person, in the order to do it, with the button that does it.

chapters.title: One line says how much is waiting
chapters.detail: And what kind, so you know whether it is bugs to fix or a connection to repair.

chapters.title: Work from the top down
chapters.detail: Each card says what is wrong and what to do, with a button to the page where you do it.

chapters.title: Broken connections show up here too
chapters.detail: An expired key stops bugs and fixes moving. Reconnect it from its card.

chapters.title: Filter by stage
chapters.detail: Plan, Do, Check, Act and Ops: see which part of the loop is stuck.
